question: In Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY), testosterone replacement therapy should be started at the onset of puberty to promote virilisation and prevent the metabolic and psychological consequences of androgen deficiency; gynaecomastia in these patients also carries an increased risk of breast cancer compared with 46,XY males.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Both parts of this statement are true. Testosterone replacement is the cornerstone of Klinefelter management and should begin at the start of expected puberty. Gynaecomastia is common (due to relative oestrogen excess) and does carry an elevated breast cancer risk — approximately 20 times that of 46,XY males — making surveillance relevant.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Testosterone replacement in Klinefelter syndrome is initiated at the time of expected puberty onset (typically ~11–12 years) using depot or transdermal preparations, titrated to achieve mid-normal adult testosterone levels. This promotes virilisation, prevents osteoporosis, and improves mood and energy. Gynaecomastia, present in ~50–75%, results from the elevated oestrogen-to-testosterone ratio and does confer a ~20-fold higher breast cancer risk than 46,XY males — annual breast self-examination is recommended.
